title: Reading Sample Fluorescence (PDMPO) via Fluorometer
author: Brittany N Zepernick
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.72whqfe

steps.title: Configure Fluorometer Measurement Mode
steps.instruction: Set up the device measurement parameters from the home screen.

substeps.instruction: Confirm the machine reads 'simple multi-operational' and press ENTER.
Use arrow buttons to select 'Direct concentration' and press ENTER.
Select the 'units' button and choose the appropriate unit (e.g., mg/L, mg/mL, ng/mL) based on the standards used.

steps.title: Set Concentration Range and Standards Count
steps.instruction: Define the expected concentration range and the number of standards for calibration.

substeps.instruction: Press ESCAPE to return to the main home screen.
Select 'max range' and enter the maximum approximate concentration range expected (this may require trial and error based on cell concentration, incubation conditions, and filtered volume).
Enter the number of standards being used (e.g., 5) and press ENTER.

steps.title: Calibrate Fluorometer with Standards
steps.instruction: Perform the calibration process using the standard solutions.

substeps.instruction: Pipet 4 mL of the highest standard into a disposable glass 10 mL tube, wipe the outside of the tube, and insert it into the machine.
Enter the concentration of the standard in the previously selected units, select 'OK', and press '*' to read the standard.
Repeat the pipetting and reading process for the remaining standards.

steps.title: Insert Blank Sample
steps.instruction: Calibrate the machine using a blank solution.

substeps.instruction: Follow the prompt to insert a blank consisting of 4 mL of NaOH and 1 mL 1M HCl, then press ENTER.

steps.title: Prepare and Read Samples
steps.instruction: Measure the fluorescence of the processed samples.

substeps.instruction: Carefully pipette the top 4 mL of matrix from recently centrifuged samples into a clean 10 mL disposable glass tube, ensuring the bottom of the 15 mL Falcon tube (containing filter fragments and unlysed/digested cells) is not disturbed.
Press the '*' button to begin the sample reading; the resulting number on the computer screen is an average of various fluorescence measurements.

steps.title: Calculate PDMPO and Silica Concentrations
steps.instruction: Convert fluorescence readings (FSU) to actual concentrations using linear regression.

substeps.instruction: Use the linear regression equation (where FSU is y and concentration is x) to solve for the actual concentration of PDMPO.
Ensure the linear regression equation has an R² value > 0.95 (R² > 0.99 preferred).
Convert the actual concentration from mL/nL to mol.
Convert PDMPO concentration to silica using the conversion factor 3230:1 for Si:PDMPO (mol:mol).

steps.title: Normalize and Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Normalize the silica data to obtain final values.

substeps.instruction: Normalize the results to either cells/mL or chlorophyll-A data for each sample to obtain Si (mol)/cell.
Graph the information to show silica deposition rates over time.
